newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot resids mostly steady, NYH HSFO firms.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot resids mostly steady, NYH HSFO firms.

text.p: U.S. spot fuel oil prices again held mostly steady Wednesday in thin trade, but strong East Coast bunkers and colder weather in the region helped firm New York Harbor high sulphur material, sources said.
"(Firm) bunkers are holding high sulphur up. The market feels a little better supported," said one cash trader, adding the market felt steady to firmer provided crude remains stable.
In New York Harbor, three percent gained 25-50 cents to near $14 a barrel on strong East Coast bunkers, but traders said U.S. Gulf Coast three percent at about $13.25 registered no change Wednesday.
NYH physical one percent again was unchanged at $15.25-50, with prompt barges quoted at the high end of the range.
NYH May one percent paper was up slightly to the $15.30-35 area despite softer crude. Traders said June paper was quoted 10-15 cents over May.
NYH 2.2 percent notionally held steady at $14.00-25.
U.S. Gulf one percent remained pegged at $15.00-25, traders said.
No NYH or USG deals were reported.

On Wednesday, New York city gate swing gas prices again firmed by about five cents to the low-to-mid $2.40s/mmBtu, or $15.44 a barrel equivalent, due to well-below normal temperatures in the area. Gas at Henry Hub, the NYMEX delivery point, slipped a nickel to the mid-$1.90s/mmBtu, or $12.29 a barrel.
